what_it_does: Quantum computers are approaching the scale where a single device cannot hold all the qubits needed for a useful computation, so researchers envision quantum data centers — buildings full of quantum processor chips connected by a fiber-optic network with reconfigurable optical switches that can redirect light paths between racks. The problem is that reconfiguring an optical switch is slow, so every time two distant quantum processors need to communicate, there can be a long pause. SwitchQNet is a compiler that plans both the quantum operations and the network switch schedule at the same time: it reorders and batches quantum gate communications so that many operations share a single switch configuration, spreading the reconfiguration cost across multiple transfers. It also accounts for quantum error correction to target fault-tolerant execution.
